goal: Classify how the MNIST network's 32-bit fixed-point requantization clamps a scaled accumulator into a uint8 activation code, so no activation ever leaves 0 to 255.

app.name: mnist-requant-clamp
app.title: Requantization clamp
app.purpose: Classify the scaled accumulator q of one requantized activation, from its sign and magnitude, as clamped to the floor 0, passed through unchanged, or clamped to the ceiling 255.

fields.name: sign
fields.means: the sign of q = ((acc + bias) * M + 2^31 + Z * 2^32) quot 2^32

fields.name: q
fields.means: the magnitude of q, bounded by the 32-bit fixed-point range

meanings.floor: q is below 0 and the code is 0, the uint8 zero point
meanings.passed: q is already a uint8 code and is kept
meanings.ceiling: q is above 255 and the code is 255

rules.why: src/Mnist/Core.lex.tex requant: lo = if q < 0 then 0 else q
src/Mnist/Core.lex.tex requant: hi = if 255 < lo then 255 else lo

app.otherwiseWhy: src/Mnist/Core.lex.tex requant: a q in 0..255 is returned as the activation code; README.md: uint8 activations with zero point 0

properties.why: a negative accumulator never becomes a positive code
an in-range code is never altered

stakeholders.name: Model auditor
stakeholders.text: Checks that the LexLean network computes exactly what mnist-12-int8.onnx computes, layer by layer.

stakeholders.name: Package integrator
stakeholders.text: Embeds the certified rust-std mnist package and needs every activation to be a uint8 code.

components.name: onnxruntime
components.text: onnxruntime 1.29.0, whose class on all 10,000 test images is the authority (MN-05).

components.name: mnist package
components.text: The certified rust-std package in dist/ exporting run(Bytes).

threats.name: Activation wraps past 255
threats.text: A large accumulator is truncated to 8 bits instead of saturating, changing the class.

evidence.reference: UOR-Foundation/MNIST MN-05: class equal to onnxruntime on 10,000 images

threats.name: Negative activation
threats.text: A negative accumulator passes as a large unsigned code.

threats.name: Accumulator overflow
threats.text: The accumulator itself overflows before requantization.
threats.accepted: README.md says so: that the accumulators never overflow is not a theorem; the overflow effect stays declared and checked at every operation.

quality.measureText: The largest code any request is answered with.

quality.text: The package returns onnxruntime's class on every test image, as MN-05 gates.
quality.measureText: Test images whose class differs from onnxruntime 1.29.0.
